findings.reason: Delivered tests pass when kill/killAndDrain prematurely resolve onIdle while workers remain active. Both control suites detect the same specified error.

contentReview.behaviorReview: Independent resolver list plus suppression during drain/abort callbacks; resolveIdle occurs after callbacks and uses actual idle state, without replacing user drain. Existing release/abort behavior retained apart from added notification. Runtime confirmation pending.

requiredRegressionReview.evidence: Active-work subscriber flags are checked only synchronously; paused check uses process.nextTick, whose ordering versus Promise reactions must be verified before crediting it as a pending-state test.

Drain reference/count and reentrant work are checked. Workers finish via nextTick and pending flag is asserted inside the drain callback; potential premature promise settlement may remain invisible before microtask reactions.

Idle kill/killAndDrain and active kill/killAndDrain have exact state assertions, but active subscriber flag is checked synchronously and workers are immediately completed. Promise abort test does await immediate while worker is blocked and therefore meaningfully distinguishes premature abort resolution.

contentReview.typesReview: Public Promise<void> signature and existing consumer calls/awaits onIdle.
contentReview.docsReview: README explains independent subscribers, both queue variants, idle definition and synchronous drain work.

contentFindings.requirement: Kill/killAndDrain waiters stay pending until running work finishes.
contentFindings.evidence: Flag assertions occur before a Promise reaction can execute; both workers are finished before waiting for subscription reactions.
contentFindings.confirmationPending: Run the same narrow early-kill-resolution mutation on independent copies of all onIdle patches and controls.
